chapter_title: Improving a Resource with AI Agents
learning_objective: The learner will examine seven change log entries and name the one field that is missing from each, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** change-log-gap-finder
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine seven change log entries and name the one field that is missing from each, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Change Log Entry, Human Review of Changes, Accept Correct or Reject (all defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 14). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each entry the learner commits the missing field from a list of seven. A choice is correct when it matches the Missing field column in Content. Mastery is at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. Reading the field list is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A log needs only what changed. (2) Naming the reviewer is optional. (3) The reason for a change can be guessed later. **Instructional Rationale:** Examining an entry for a missing part is an Analyze-level action. Seven entries that each lack a different field teach the learner what each field contributes. **Content:** The seven fields: When, Where, What changed, Why, Made by, Reviewed by, Decision. The seven entries (all made up for Watershed Basics). A dash marks the missing field: | # | When | Where | What changed | Why | Made by | Reviewed by | Decision | Missing field | Why it matters (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | - | Section 2, paragraph 1 | "410 miles" became "398 miles" | Outdated figure | Agent | Reviewer A | Accepted | When | Without a date, no one can tell which version was scored. | | 2 | 2026-10-24 | - | "410 miles" became "398 miles" | Outdated figure | Agent | Reviewer A | Accepted | Where | A reuser cannot find the change. | | 3 | 2026-10-24 | Image 3 | - | One-word alt text | Agent | Reviewer A | Corrected | What changed | A reuser must be able to indicate what was changed. | | 4 | 2026-10-24 | Link 9 | Address replaced | - | Person | Reviewer A | Accepted | Why | The change cannot be tied to the check it fixes. | | 5 | 2026-10-24 | Heading 4 | Level 4 became level 3 | Skipped heading level | - | Reviewer A | Accepted | Made by | The log cannot show how often agents are right. | | 6 | 2026-10-24 | Question 3 | Explanation added | No explanation | Agent | - | Accepted | Reviewed by | Nothing shows that a person checked the change. | | 7 | 2026-10-24 | Section 3 | Sentence shortened | Reading level | Agent | Reviewer A | - | Decision | No one can tell whether the change was kept. | **Provenance:** The entries are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The seven fields follow the chapter section "Change Log Entry". **Rules:** Each entry lacks exactly one field, and each of the seven fields is missing from exactly one entry. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one entry as a row with one empty cell. 2. The learner chooses which of the seven fields is missing, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After entry 7 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 7 entries in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [field]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The missing field is [field]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 7 correct on the first attempt". At 6 or more it adds "You can read a change log." Below 6 it lists the Why text of each missed entry. **Starting State:** The first entry in the shuffled order and the list of seven fields. The question shown is "Which field is missing?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists seven questions that a log entry answers, and gives three complete entries for the running example.
